note: Rebuilt on every run of .github/workflows/daily-creator-pull.yml from the hooks harvested that day. Spyglass HOOK/USP aggregation returns empty for these creators because it is tuned to paid campaigns, so the patterns are read off the organic hooks themselves. Every quote is verified against a harvested hook before it is written.

patterns.label: drops you into a live question
patterns.description: Opens on the interviewer's question rather than the answer, so the viewer arrives as an eavesdropper on a conversation already in progress. The pending answer is the pull.

examples.creator: Michael Llanas
examples.quote: I really want to deep dive into owner financing because I know that's what you specialize in

examples.creator: 𝘾𝘼𝙈𝙀𝙍𝙊𝙉 𝙊𝙇𝙄𝙑𝙀𝙍𝘼  📍ℂ𝕙𝕚𝕔𝕒𝕘𝕠
examples.quote: I guess what areas do you invest in, how frequently?

examples.creator: Ravi Sharma
examples.quote: So how do you adapt post budget around building wealth with property?

examples.creator: Sean Pan
examples.quote: Does it matter if you intend to have like housemates and stuff like that?

examples.creator: Jerry Norton
examples.quote: What would a package deal look like if I bought this and Iowa?

patterns.label: opens by naming a new rule
patterns.description: Leads with a specific piece of legislation, policy change or market shift by name, betting the viewer feels behind on something that affects their money. The unfamiliar proper noun creates an information gap that must be closed.

examples.creator: Scott Betley
examples.quote: Hey Kyle, have you heard about the MOVE Act that Congress just proposed that can help homeowners keep their lower interest rates?

examples.creator: Scott Kuru
examples.quote: If the government's new SMSF property rules have got you thinking, "Fine, I can't borrow for residential anymore. I'll just buy commercial."

examples.creator: Ravi Sharma
examples.quote: Okay, mortgage wars have kicked off, and for anyone that doesn't know what that means, it could be really good news for you and the repayments on your house.

patterns.label: leads with the finished number
patterns.description: States an already-achieved outcome attached to a hard dollar figure or ranking before explaining anything. The proof arrives first, so the only remaining question is how it was done.

examples.creator: Sean Pan
examples.quote: I bought this 4plex for $250,000 and this is how much I make from it.

examples.creator: Jack Henderson
examples.quote: We just finished building it, and we made a sneaky, "one and a half million bucks" along the way.

examples.creator: Jeremy Werden
examples.quote: Five years ago, we turned this into North Carolina's number one Airbnb.

patterns.label: says the search query aloud
patterns.description: The hook is the bare question or how-to phrase someone would type into a search bar, with no framing at all. It matches intent instantly for anyone already looking for that answer.

examples.creator: Logan Fullmer
examples.quote: How to find houses for cheap.

examples.creator: Jack Henderson
examples.quote: How to become a young... investor.

examples.creator: Fernando Gonzalez
examples.quote: ¿Cómo empezar a invertir en bienes raíces?

patterns.label: starts in the middle of talking
patterns.description: Begins mid-sentence or mid-lesson, complete with filler words, as though the camera caught an ongoing session. The implied missing context makes the clip feel like leaked material rather than a produced intro.

examples.creator: Jerry Norton
examples.quote: Okay, so the next thing I need to talk about some earnest money, man,

examples.creator: Michael Llanas
examples.quote: The calling listings that have been on the market for a long time.

examples.creator: Logan Fullmer
examples.quote: Why do I care?

patterns.label: voices the doubt before answering
patterns.description: Opens by stating the pessimistic or dismissive belief the audience already holds, sometimes in the doubter's own voice, before the creator has said a word in their own. Being accurately quoted keeps people watching for the rebuttal.

examples.creator: Ravi Sharma
examples.quote: Prices are falling and people are freaking out

examples.creator: Scott Betley
examples.quote: I got a buyer right now with a 3 % down payment and they want to wait a year because they think buying a home right now is stupid.

examples.creator: Fernando Gonzalez
examples.quote: Ay, es que necesito ser rico para comenzar a invertir en bienes raíces.

patterns.label: points at a thing on screen
patterns.description: Uses a physical gesture word — this, here — to make the viewer look at an object or place in frame before any claim is made. Curiosity about what is being pointed at does the work.

examples.creator: Erick Brice
examples.quote: This is your house This is your house Hey

examples.creator: Jack Henderson
examples.quote: You see this little house here?

examples.creator: Logan Fullmer
examples.quote: One of the best places in all the land to buy distressed property is right here, your county courthouse.

patterns.label: casts you in the scene
patterns.description: Assigns the viewer a role, age or moment in second person and speaks as if it is already happening to them. It removes the choice of whether the topic is relevant.

examples.creator: Erick Brice
examples.quote: You're 20 years old.

examples.creator: Emeline SIRON - Experte investissement immobilier
examples.quote: Cette nuit, tu vas gagner de l'argent en dormant.

examples.creator: Theoni Rapo
examples.quote: When a seller accepts your offer for a house, there are typically three things that you pay for within a week of that offer being accepted.

patterns.label: pushes back on accepted wisdom
patterns.description: Opens by denying something the audience assumes is true or mocking the language insiders repeat, creating a small argument the viewer has to see resolved. Disagreement is the hook, not information.

examples.creator: Jeremy Werden
examples.quote: Your rental property does not need an oversized closet that nobody's using.

examples.creator: Jerry Norton
examples.quote: Although wholesaling as a strategy may be simple to understand, it isn't easy to execute.

examples.creator: Sean Pan
examples.quote: Real estate investors love throwing around terms like cash on cash return.

patterns.label: warns you off, withholds why
patterns.description: Issues a caution to someone about to act or already exposed, then defers the actual reason to the body of the video. The threat is named but the explanation is hostage.

examples.creator: Jeremy Werden
examples.quote: Do not buy a lakefront or beachfront property unless you consider this.

examples.creator: Scott Kuru
examples.quote: If you own property in Australia, you need to understand just how much the tax office can actually see about you,

patterns.label: states what they own first
patterns.description: Establishes standing by naming the portfolio, market or students taught before any advice is given. The claim to be worth listening to precedes the content.

examples.creator: Avery Carl
examples.quote: I own a bunch of short -term rentals on 30A and in Destin, Florida,

examples.creator: Michael Llanas
examples.quote: So the students in Hustle Academy, we teach exactly this method about taking on people's payments.

patterns.label: puts a future year in the question
patterns.description: Poses a plain question but stamps it with a year that hasn't happened yet, positioning the answer as forecast rather than history. Anyone planning ahead cannot skip it. Single example.

examples.creator: Avery Carl
examples.quote: How much will an Airbnb make in 2026?

patterns.label: invites you into a money challenge
patterns.description: Frames the video as a joint attempt to hit a dollar amount inside a stated timeframe, using "let's" or a repeatable routine. It turns a lesson into a live experiment with a scoreboard. Single example.

examples.creator: 𝘾𝘼𝙈𝙀𝙍𝙊𝙉 𝙊𝙇𝙄𝙑𝙀𝙍𝘼  📍ℂ𝕙𝕚𝕔𝕒𝕘𝕠
examples.quote: Let's have AI make us 10 grand in two weeks.

patterns.label: opens inside a real phone call
patterns.description: Starts with the first line of an actual call to a stranger, naming them and their address, so the viewer is watching the thing happen rather than hearing it described. Single example.

examples.creator: Jerry Norton
examples.quote: Hi Peter, my name is Jerry Norton calling you about your property on Liberty Road.
